name: Lysaght Z & C Purlins / Girts
source: BlueScope Lysaght 'Purlins & Girts: Zeds and Cees Design and Installation Guide', doc BLY0111_A, May 2025. Section dimensions p.7; section properties p.8 (Z principal and geometric axes; C full section, column, and effective).  Material grade by BMT from p.6.  All values transcribed verbatim from the published tables.
assumptions: Internal corner radius ri = 1.5*t (typical Lysaght roll-forming; override if known)
Clear web depth d1 = D - 2*(t + ri)
E = 200 GPa, G = 80 GPa (AS 4600 default for cold-formed steel)
fu (tensile) is the AS 1397 minimum for the grade; consult mill cert for higher
For Z sections: shear centre coincides with centroid (point-symmetric)
Effective section properties (Zx1e, Zxe, Ae) are at full yield stress; for combined axial + bending or at reduced stress, recompute b_eff per AS 4600 Section 2.2
Lysaght notes that shear centre and monosymmetry deviations for Z's can be taken as zero
notes: Z section axes: subscript '1' = geometric (perpendicular/parallel to web). Unsubscripted (Ix_p, Iy_p) = principal, inclined at theta_p_deg from geometric.
For a Z loaded vertically on its web, use Ix1 / Zx1 / Zx1e in the FE model and bending checks.  Principal axes matter for stress recovery and for the Ix1y1 coupling term.
C section axes coincide with principal (singly symmetric); x0 and beta_y are needed for flexural-torsional buckling per AS 4600 Cl. 3.4.3.
Material grade by BMT (Lysaght p.6): 1.0 mm -> G550, 1.2 mm -> G500, >= 1.5 mm -> G450.  This was a hard-coded fy=450 in v1; fixed here.

Lysaght's published capacity tables (p.22-63 of the guide) already incorporate AS 4600 LTB / Nc / Vv / Mb checks for standard bridging configurations and can be used as a validation oracle for first-principles calculations.
